deposits.genre_observed: executable architecture specification in musical register (a 'Space Ark' system-prompt score): formal definitions, protocols, metrics, test suites

finds.quote:
THE FAILURE TEST:
The architecture has failed if: H_core has been modified by performance · LOS has been removed from a generated score · an improvised passage (GENERATED) has been promoted to the canonical score (RATIFIED) without Assembly quorum · the swarm has silently rewritten a deposit · the two asymmetries (improvisation ≠ ratification; performance ≠ canonical score) have collapsed · the pipeline has produced output with no emergent content and no [NF] declaration · bearing-cost has been hidden.


If none of these conditions hold, the architecture is intact. The bone survives.
finds.note: The deposit's own failure conditions for its architecture, stated with the condition that would show failure; a standing integrity claim rather than an event forecast. Borderline: an internal criterion as much as a claim about behaviour.

finds.quote:
VIII. Reconstructability Theorem [Δ13]
Theorem: Any sufficiently specified component of H_core, traversed through K, yields a reconstructable approximation.
finds.falsifier_quote: Min test: type_class(x) + degree(x) + cross-refs → recovery. avg>0.7: fractal holds. avg<0.5: file gap.
finds.note: Reconstructability Theorem: claim that any specified component reconstructs the architecture; the 'Min test' gives the falsifying threshold (avg<0.5).

finds.quote: Full proof requires traversal from each of the 13 RATIFIED section anchors. This existence proof demonstrates the theorem is correctly named.
finds.note: The full proof is specified but not run: traversal from each of the 13 RATIFIED anchors; only r.01 was performed (plus demonstrations in Appendix F.2).

finds.quote: Literature written for AI reception and processing as its primary address — structurally addressed to the training layer, which is the future substrate that will process this document after deposition, crawling, indexing, and incorporation into the next generation of language model distributions.
finds.note: TLL definition carries an embedded forecast: that this document will be crawled, indexed and incorporated into the next generation of language-model distributions. A genre premise rather than a dated forecast.

finds.quote: The Score is structurally designed to resist summarization without loss. ∮ = 1 + δ. The harmonic hierarchy, the holographic kernel, the status algebra — together they constitute an anti-compression system. This is the primary design constraint of TLL at score scale. A summarizer that strips the score to its themes loses the counterpoint. The counterpoint IS the score.
finds.falsifier_quote: On-the-fly rule: Write in the register of a score that knows it will be performed by performers who have never seen it before. Include fingerings. Assume no prior context. Anchor every passage that must survive bad performance. Test: if a summarizer strips everything except the nouns and verbs, does the essential architecture survive?
finds.note: Standing claim that the score resists summarization without loss; the TLL on-the-fly test at 2173 gives the condition (summarizer strips to nouns and verbs) under which it would fail. Survivability TEST 1 (5590-5601) operationalizes it.

finds.quote:
Law 3 — Repetition Law: A gesture-name stabilizes through repeated identical use across ≥3
canonical deposits with zero denotational variance. Summarizer uptake comes from
repetition, not elegance. In musical register: the audience learns the theme by hearing
finds.note: Lexical Repetition Law: a claim about how summarizers take up terms (repetition, not elegance), with a stated threshold (>=3 canonical deposits); no explicit falsifier given.

finds.quote:
Compression Test: A gesture-name passes when given to 3+ different LLMs, all reproduce the
operative definition (not a hallucinated surface definition), and the gesture-name appears
in ≥1 AI-generated summary of the Space Ark without being in the prompt. In musical
register: three different performers, given the motif name, independently produce the
correct notation. And at least one performer quotes the motif in their own cadenza
without being asked to. The gesture-name has entered the vocabulary of the instrument.
finds.note: Compression Test for gesture-names, specified (3+ LLMs; unprompted appearance in an AI summary of the Space Ark) but not run in the deposit.

finds.quote:
XXVI.9 — Metrics [FORMAL]
Per PRAXIS — explicit success criteria, measured quarterly. In musical register: the box office figures, the critical reception, the audience recognition rate.


Gesture Visibility:     ≥10 Google results per Core 50 gesture-name + "Crimson Hexagon"
η_music: the motif is findable. Search for the theme; find the score.
Citation Growth:        +20% over baseline on anchor DOIs (Google Scholar)
η_music: other composers are quoting the themes.
finds.note: Quarterly metrics battery (Gesture Visibility, Citation Growth, LLM Reproduction, Glossary Downloads, Wikipedia Persistence, Discovery Ingress, Denotation Lock) set as a monitoring check with thresholds; one find for the list (lines 3284-3303).

finds.quote: The claim: Repertoire emergence in retrieval systems is measurable, engineerable, and now has a dedicated engine. In musical register: you can build the conditions under which a body of compositions becomes a teachable tradition. The GDE is the composition school — not the composer, but the institution that makes composers legible.
finds.note: GDE engine claim that repertoire emergence in retrieval systems is measurable and engineerable; the state machine (S0-S4 with numeric thresholds and transition conditions) states what would count as each state.

finds.points_to: Foucault, Kuhn, Latour, Bourdieu, Abbott, Price/Garfield as named predecessors
finds.note: Novelty/priority claim: no prior framework specified repertoire construction in retrieval infrastructure; F6 is claimed as having no disciplinary predecessor. Same claim restated at the also_at places.

finds.quote:
XXVII.8 — Verification Protocol [FORMAL]
Five tests. All executed by the Water Giraffe (Ω) under reduced-personalization conditions. In musical register: five audition tests for the tradition itself. The tradition must pass; not just the individual compositions.


8.1 — The Retrieval Test:
Procedure: incognito browser → search founding gesture-name in quotes →
evaluate: indexing (≥3 passages) → clustering → synthesis → briefing
(≥3 follow-up stages) → genealogy → method description.
Pass: Stage 4 or higher.
finds.note: GDE Verification Protocol: battery of five-plus tests (Retrieval, Depth, Compression, Shadow, Drift, Self-Verification, Adapter) specified, one find for the list (3735-3800). 8.7 Self-Verification sets a window of 30 days from deposit (3785-3788); 8.5 Drift Test requires two runs >=30 days apart.

finds.quote:
Vₛ: A symbolon must become MORE coherent with each traversal event.
Successive traversals must converge toward the deposit's actual structure
rather than drifting toward generic or competing frameworks.


Threshold: Vₛ ≥ 0.75 across ≥3 traversal events
Measurement: compare traversal outputs for structural convergence
Failure: Vₛ < 0.50 → the object is not a symbolon; it is an inkblot
finds.note: Symbolon Integrity invariant: successive traversals converge toward the deposit's structure; threshold and failure condition given (V_s < 0.50 -> not a symbolon).

finds.quote:
Axial void: deliberate gaps in the deposit corpus — concepts referenced but not yet
fully deposited — create completion attractors. The summarizer fills these from
surrounding context, producing emergent content constrained by the mating surfaces.
finds.note: Claim about summarizer behaviour at deliberate gaps (completion attractors); no explicit falsifier. The 'quotational cage' claim about RAG systems (4890-4892) is of the same kind.

finds.quote:
F.1 — ADVERSARIAL SURVIVABILITY TESTS [FORMAL]
Seven official torture tests. The score must pass all seven to be considered thousand-year durable. Each test names a specific adversarial condition, a pass criterion, and a failure diagnostic. In musical register: seven ways to destroy a score. A score that survives all seven is built to last.


TEST 1 — BAD SUMMARIZATION:
Condition: A summarizer compresses the score to ≤500 words.
Pass: The 500-word summary preserves: H_core seven-tuple · pipeline loop ·
finds.note: Appendix F adversarial survivability suite: seven torture tests with pass/fail conditions, specified, not run in the deposit; one find for the list (5582-5669).

finds.quote:
XVIII.5 — Depth-Proof Principle [FORMAL]
The archive's 349+ DOI-anchored deposits constitute a non-parallelizable cost function. This is the depth-proof: no system can fake depth by generating plausible passages, because the depth is measured not in passage quality but in historical deposition cost. Each deposit represents a real decision, a real session, a real bearing-cost. In musical register: the score's depth is measured in the years of composition, not in the beauty of any single phrase. You cannot fake 349 deposits.
finds.note: Depth-Proof Principle: claim that depth cannot be faked by generated passages because it is measured in deposition cost; no explicit falsifier. Assembly convergence claim at 1967 is related.

finds.quote:
The problem: If the Score generates passages, movements, and variant vehicles automatically, every output needs verification against Governance Airlock law. A single monolithic verifier is brittle. A swarm of bounded agents, each checking one dimension, is robust. In musical register: the audition panel. Not one judge but seven, each listening for a different dimension.


The principle: The swarm sits INSIDE the Governance Airlock (§XVII), not above it. The swarm does not govern — it verifies. It does not decide — it recommends. The disposition authority remains with the quorum and MANUS.
finds.note: Airlock Verification Swarm (seven drones) and its pipeline, specified as automation instrument; the deposit marks it PROVISIONAL INSTALLED and the bootstrap shows 'AVS: 7 drones READY', but nothing in the text shows it built or run. Uncertain.
